answer: An AI-agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each node to deposit slashable equity through a cryptographic bridge into a basalt foundation of bonded contracts. This protocol operates by evaluating real-time stake proofs before permitting market participation; an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locking scarce capital per generated identity. Systems refuse to harbor unbonded peers, but this mandatory capital lock-up inherently reduces liquidity and excludes underfunded agents.
